title: Failure Ledger
description: A permanent, append-only public record of what we tried and what didn't work. Every entry is dated, honest, and irreversible. The purpose is accountability: you should be able to see our mistakes as clearly as our successes.

entries.title: PPDA-based expected offsides (xO) metric abandoned
entries.what_we_tried: Built an expected offsides model using PPDA (Passes Per Defensive Action) as a key feature, hypothesizing that high-pressing teams generate more offside traps.
entries.what_happened: The FootyStats API does not provide PPDA data. Confirmed against 1,140 real matches across multiple leagues. The field simply doesn't exist in the data source.
entries.conclusion: Abandoned entirely. No alternative data source identified at acceptable cost. The hypothesis remains plausible but untestable with our data.

entries.title: Goals over/under model initially underperformed naive baseline
entries.what_we_tried: Applied the same count-regression approach that works for corners to the goals over/under 2.5 market.
entries.what_happened: Initial performance was -4.1% vs naive baseline with ECE of 0.090. After applying shrinkage correction to the team-strength estimates, performance improved to +0.2% — roughly at par with the naive baseline.
entries.conclusion: The goals model is NOT claimed as an edge. It's approximately at par (+0.2%) which is statistically indistinguishable from zero advantage. We do not market this as a product.

entries.title: BTTS (Both Teams To Score) model at par, not an edge
entries.what_we_tried: Applied count-regression to the BTTS market, expecting similar outperformance to corners.
entries.what_happened: Performance settled at +0.4% vs naive baseline. Statistically indistinguishable from zero.
entries.conclusion: BTTS is NOT claimed as an edge. It produces calibrated probabilities but no meaningful advantage over naive baselines. Honest assessment: this market may simply be more efficient than corners.

entries.title: Corners calibration silently regressed during refit-interval change
entries.what_we_tried: Changed the model's refit interval (how often it re-trains on accumulated data) as part of a routine optimization.
entries.what_happened: Corners ECE regressed from 0.018 to 0.035 without any test catching it. The regression was silent — no monitoring alert fired.
entries.conclusion: Caught and fixed. Added explicit calibration regression tests. The original 0.018 figure was from a single EPL sample and proved optimistic regardless — the multi-league reality is ~0.064. This incident revealed that we were tracking against a misleadingly good baseline.

entries.title: Market-inefficiency hypothesis DISPROVEN by our own data
entries.what_we_tried: Hypothesized that the model's edge should be larger in thinly-bet leagues (lower liquidity = less efficient market = more exploitable mispricing).
entries.what_happened: Tested across all 25 leagues in the robustness check. Edge magnitude shows no correlation with estimated league betting volume. Portugal and Netherlands perform similarly to England and Spain.
entries.conclusion: DISPROVEN. The edge appears uniform across league tiers. This is actually a robustness signal — it suggests the model captures a real structural feature (team-level corner/card tendencies) rather than exploiting a market-specific inefficiency that would disappear with liquidity.

entries.title: FDR individual-level testing: only 60/150 tests survive correction
entries.what_we_tried: Applied Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate correction to individual league-season test results (150 tests: 75 league-seasons x 2 models).
entries.what_happened: Only 60/150 individual tests survive BH correction at alpha=0.05. This reflects low per-test statistical power (100-300 matches per league-season) rather than absence of effect.
entries.conclusion: The individual tests lack power. The meta-analysis (aggregating across all league-seasons) is what passes with high confidence. We should say plainly: the evidence is in the aggregate pattern, not in any single league-season. A single league-season is too small a sample to detect the effect size we're seeing.

entries.title: Single-sample calibration figures proved optimistic
entries.what_we_tried: Initially reported ECE of 0.018 (corners) and 0.027 (cards) from an EPL-only evaluation.
entries.what_happened: Multi-league robustness check across 25 leagues and 3 seasons revealed the realistic figures are ~0.064 (corners) and ~0.058 (cards). The original numbers were an optimistic single-sample estimate.
entries.conclusion: Replaced all references to the 0.018/0.027 figures with the honest multi-league numbers (0.064/0.058). The model is still well-calibrated — ECE under 0.07 is good — but the original claim was misleadingly precise. Lesson: never report a single-sample estimate as if it's a stable parameter.

entries.title: 4 predictions unattested due to late attestation wiring
entries.what_we_tried: Quarantine started 2026-08-27 12:00 UTC. Predictions generated at 15:45 UTC. Attestation (commit-reveal) wasn't wired into the prediction loop until Aug 28.
entries.what_happened: 4 predictions (2 matches x 2 models: Celta vs Osasuna and Barcelona vs Athletic, Aug 27 evening) were generated before attestation was wired, and their matches kicked off before backfill could run. These predictions cannot be cryptographically proven to have been made pre-kickoff.
entries.conclusion: These 4 predictions are marked as UNATTESTED in the feed. They represent day-1 of the quarantine window. All subsequent predictions (190+) have valid pre-kickoff commitments. The gap is disclosed rather than hidden.

entries.title: Corners/cards quarantine retired — architecture reoriented to metric discovery
entries.what_we_tried: Enrolled two target-predictor models (Corners O/U 9.5, Cards O/U 3.5) in a 90-day quarantine on 2026-08-27. The plan was to validate individual strategy-level predictions against live fixtures.
entries.what_happened: Within 24 hours of enrollment, the architecture was reoriented from strategy-validation to metric-validation. Target predictors (which predict one specific market outcome) are not the right unit of validation — they do not compose into anything reusable. The correct primitive is a reusable metric that composes into unlimited creator hypotheses. Both models were marked SUPERSEDED after generating 194 predictions (190 attested).
entries.conclusion: The quarantine enrollments are preserved as immutable project history but predictions are no longer treated as product evidence. The modeling work (count regression with shrinkage, Dixon-Coles) carries forward directly into the metric discovery pipeline as scoring models. This is an architecture decision, not a failure of the models themselves — they were performing as expected.

entries.title: Metric discovery: first null was artifact of wrong screener — confirmed after correction
entries.what_we_tried: Ran two discovery approaches: (1) binary median-split screening of 1,398 single-feature arithmetic combinations, (2) model-based screening (L2-regularized logistic regression) of team-specific rolling features with within-league walk-forward. Both used the full corpus (7,692 discovery matches, 25 leagues, 2 seasons).
entries.what_happened: First run (binary median-split): 0/1,398 survivors — but sanity gate later showed the screener could not detect known-good signal. Second run (logistic regression): same result, same problem. Third run (Poisson GLM with shrinkage — the correct model class): sanity gate PASSED, full search found 2,752 FDR survivors on cards target (BSS up to +3.4%), all confirmed on held-out data (BSS +1.2% to +2.2%, p < 0.000003). The first two nulls were artifacts of mis-specified screeners, not absent signal.
entries.conclusion: The correct conclusion has two parts: (1) Signal IS discoverable when the screening model matches the domain structure (Poisson for count data, not logistic). (2) The discovered combinations are WEAKER than the full baseline model (+2.2% BSS vs +6.1% robustness check), confirming that model architecture matters more than feature selection — but feature selection still contributes meaningfully. The 2,752 survivors reduce to ~4 distinct patterns: team card rates + fouls/tempo features. This is ONE underlying signal (team disciplinary persistence) accessed through different feature subsets.

entries.title: Corners discovery: signal inaccessible to Poisson GLM over rolling averages (tested, not inferred)
entries.what_we_tried: Ran the proven Poisson GLM screener (which detected cards at +1.4% BSS) on corners target with team-specific rolling corner rates.
entries.what_happened: ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS (2026-08-28, now superseded): Assumed the global temporal split was the problem and per-league walk-forward would fix it. TESTED RESULT: Per-league walk-forward with team-specific rolling corner rates produces BSS = -3.6% (6/25 leagues positive). Per-league walk-forward with the ACTUAL corners model features (dangerous_attacks, attacks, possession, shots) produces BSS = -16.9% (2/23 leagues positive). BOTH approaches fail. The +6.8% robustness result relies on full team-effect estimation with shrinkage across the entire training period — a fundamentally different operation from fitting a Poisson GLM over rolling feature averages. The split method was NOT the problem.
entries.conclusion: The corners signal is architecturally bound to the CountRegressionModel's team-effect estimation (per-team Poisson rate parameters with shrinkage toward league mean). This cannot be replicated by a generic Poisson GLM over rolling averages, regardless of which features are used or how the walk-forward is split. Corners is NOT a viable target for the combination-discovery pipeline. The signal is in the model ARCHITECTURE, not in any feature combination — consistent with the earlier diagnostic finding (F010). The cards model works in the pipeline because card rates have higher team-level persistence than corner rates (confirmed: card autocorrelation > 0 vs corner autocorrelation ≈ -0.03).

entries.title: BTTS: sanity gate passes marginally but no survivors after cumulative FDR
entries.what_we_tried: Ran logistic GLM screener on BTTS target using team goal-scoring rolling rates (the natural features for BTTS prediction).
entries.what_happened: Sanity gate passed marginally (BSS = +0.22%, p = 0.097). 351 candidates passed screening but NONE survived cumulative FDR correction (family = 22,848). Best screening p-values were in the 0.01-0.05 range — too weak for a family this large.
entries.conclusion: BTTS signal is detectable but too weak to survive rigorous multiple-testing correction. This is consistent with the earlier finding that BTTS is 'roughly at par (+0.4%)' — the per-match effect size is simply too small for the combination discovery approach to pick up given the testing burden. The BTTS market may be more efficiently priced than cards/goals.

entries.title: EV Test: All 7 discovered metrics fail to beat Bet365 on calibration
entries.what_we_tried: Tested the 7 validated metrics (4 cards, 3 goals) head-to-head against cached Bet365 closing odds on 321 EPL/La Liga matches from 2024-25. Used the exact model architecture (Poisson GLM with L2 shrinkage, team-level empirical Bayes), same feature definitions and rolling windows as validated in discovery. Vig removed via multiplicative method. Walk-forward discipline: model trained only on data before the odds sample.
entries.what_happened: Market wins 13/17 comparisons on BSS. Mean delta: -2.20% BSS (market better). Cards metrics: lose at 3.5 line (model over-predicts), marginal +1-2% BSS advantage at 4.5 line but with wide CIs and negative realized returns. Goals metrics: market dominates at ALL lines (market BSS +0.5% to +4.3%, model mostly negative). Realized flat-bet ROI is negative for every metric/line combination. No confidence interval excludes zero on the positive side.
entries.conclusion: The signals are real (they beat naive baselines as validated through FDR and held-out testing) but they are ALREADY PRICED IN by the market. Bet365 incorporates team card rates, foul rates, xG, SOT conceded, and recent goal counts — the exact factors our metrics capture — plus many additional factors we do not model. The bar for exploitable edge is "beat the market," not "beat naive." These metrics clear the naive bar by +0.5-2.3% BSS but fall short of the market bar by -2.2% BSS on average. This is a valuable finding: it quantifies exactly where the bar sits.

entries.title: Disagreement-concentrated edge: DISPROVEN — model performance DEGRADES with disagreement
entries.what_we_tried: The EV test (F013) measured AVERAGE edge and found the market wins by -2.20% BSS. A concentrated edge (right on a minority of fixtures, neutral elsewhere) would be washed out by that average. Thesis: edge is concentrated in matches where the model and market most diverge (narrative mispricing). Test: re-slice the EXACT same per-match model probabilities and vig-adjusted market probabilities by disagreement = |model_p_over - market_fair_p_over|, bucket by disagreement magnitude, and ask who is right in the highest-disagreement matches. Zero API calls. No model substitution, no refit, no retune — the analysis script imports scripts/ev_test_metrics_vs_bet365.py verbatim. Per-combo QUINTILES (per-combo n=70-281 too thin for deciles); POOLED DECILES on within-combo z-scored disagreement (3,088 rows from ~321 unique matches).
entries.what_happened: The fatal pattern the brief anticipated. Performance DEGRADES with disagreement. Pooled decile correlation (bucket index vs model-minus-market BSS) = -0.56. Lowest-disagreement decile is a dead heat with the market (+0.04% BSS); the highest-disagreement decile collapses to -14.48% BSS, directional accuracy 41% (model is closer to the actual outcome than the market LESS than half the time), follow-disagreement flat-bet ROI -18.1% [95% CI -29.9, -5.7] (CI excludes zero on the losing side). Per-combo: 8/17 DEGRADE, 8/17 FLAT, only 1/17 IMPROVES. Degradation is near-monotone on goals at high lines (goals_count_xg@3.5 corr -0.93, goals_sot_xg@3.5 -0.87, goals_sot_count@3.5 -0.76). The single IMPROVES slice (cards_minimal_pair@4.5, corr +0.64) is exactly what multiple-comparison risk predicts from 17 slices — the other three cards metrics at the same 4.5 line are FLAT. Top-decile directional split: BOTH sides lose, and the model is WORSE on the UNDER side (dir acc 37%, ROI -19.7% [-35.6, -3.1]) than the OVER side — the REVERSE of what the narrative-bias mechanism predicts. High-disagreement fixtures are predominantly EPL promoted/relegation-threatened/high-variance sides (Southampton, Ipswich, Wolves, Everton), NOT marquee derbies, with no referee concentration.
entries.conclusion: DISPROVEN, in the most damaging way. Disagreement is ANTI-informative: the model is most wrong exactly where it is most confident the market is wrong — the signature of a mis-specified model (extreme lambda estimates driven by unreliable rolling averages on thin/volatile team histories), not concealed edge. This explains WHY the EV-test average looked only mildly negative: the low-disagreement majority is a near dead-heat with the market and dilutes the concentrated losses in the high-disagreement tail. The loss is concentrated, not the edge. CAVEATS: wide CIs (~30 unique matches per bucket); this is a subset analysis on already-examined data (multiple-comparison risk); pooled rows are non-independent (one fixture spans multiple metric/line combos, so pooled CIs understate correlation). The finding must be confirmed on held-out/fresh matches before being treated as a stable property: rerun the identical disagreement-decile analysis with the frozen model on a different season or additional leagues. A self-damaging pattern is less likely to be a fluke than a positive one, but confirmation is still required.

entries.title: Championship down-tier inefficiency thesis: NOT SUPPORTED (market ~as sharp as EPL) + sanity gate failed on slice
entries.what_we_tried: Bought a complete balanced slice of English Championship (comp_8321) 25/26 via TheStatsAPI to test whether a second-tier league is more loosely priced than EPL, and whether the 7 validated metrics or new-field candidates beat that market. Cached 552 fixture stats + Bet365 odds on a balanced 200-match subset (every team 16-17 appearances, spread across all 10 months). Reused the exact Poisson-GLM+L2+shrinkage model verbatim via a schema adapter (no refit/retune/substitution); within-season point-in-time walk-forward. Ran a sanity gate, the 7 existing metrics as-is, and 7 mechanism-motivated new-field candidates (defending-block->cards, territory/crosses->corners, big-chances/npxG->goals). Cumulative FDR family 22848 -> 22855.
entries.what_happened: (1) MARKET CALIBRATION (model-independent, primary result): Bet365 Championship market BSS vs naive hovers ~0 at well-populated lines - goals@2.5 -0.18% (n=200), goals@3.5 +0.10%, cards@3.5 +0.10% (n=120), corners@9.5 -0.83% (n=109); overrounds EPL-like (goals ~5%, cards ~8%, corners ~8%). Larger negatives only at low-base-rate extremes (goals@0.5/@5.5, cards@4.5) where naive is hard to beat - same structure as EPL (ref ~-0.35%). Championship is NOT measurably sloppier than EPL. (2) SANITY GATE FAILED: the known team-card-rate->cards signal is not detectable on this slice (Spearman(predicted lambda, actual cards) = -0.105, p=0.13; mean-calibrated 4.21 vs 4.20 but rank-inverted). Per the standing rule, ALL model-side EV results were reported but NOT trusted. (3) No candidate credibly beats the market: the one eye-catching cell (cards@3.5 model-market BSS +10-12%) is a small-sample artifact of a wildly negative MARKET BSS at n=28-50; on the n=120 calibration set market BSS is +0.10%; every realized-ROI 95% CI spans zero.
entries.conclusion: The down-tier inefficiency thesis is NOT supported by this slice: a second-tier league did not price more loosely than EPL at the lines that matter. The metrics did not transfer (sanity gate failed), so no model-side edge could even be trusted. RECOMMENDATION: do NOT buy the ~10k-15k-request paid plan on this thesis. Cheap next check within the EXISTING trial (~8,660 requests remain of 10,000): re-run the identical pipeline on Championship 24/25 (sn_2930227) / 23/24 to test whether the sanity-gate failure is a single-season artifact and whether market BSS stays ~0 across seasons. BUDGET CORRECTION: the trial is metered at ~10,000 monthly requests (not the ~425 assumed), with a 12 req/min burst cap; the slice used 768 live requests.

evidence.buy_recommendation: DO NOT BUY (thesis unsupported); cheap multi-season re-check available within existing trial

entries.title: Championship sanity-gate failure is a GENERALIZATION finding, not a pipeline bug — card signal has near-zero within-season persistence on Championship 25/26
entries.what_we_tried: The Championship slice (F015) reported a sanity-gate failure: Spearman(predicted card-lambda, realized cards) = -0.105. Because a slightly-inverse correlation on independently-validated signal usually indicates a wiring bug (4 of the prior 5 sanity-gate failures were instrument mis-specification), we ran 4 diagnostics on the CACHED data (zero API calls; no model/metric/definition changes; no re-run with adjustments): (1) field-by-field schema-adapter verification + home/away orientation trace; (2) run identical feature-extraction code on known-good FootyStats corpus vs the TheStatsAPI-adapter output; (3) break the correlation down by available team history (thin-history pathology); (4) target-variable definition + reds handling.
entries.what_happened: DECISIVE RAW-FEATURE TEST (bypasses GLM/shrinkage entirely): team recent yellow-card rate -> total cards is Spearman +0.177 (p~1e-98, n=13,992) on FootyStats corpus but -0.044 (p=0.47, n=275) on Championship; recent FOUL rate -> cards is +0.170 vs -0.012; w10 yellow-rate +0.198 vs -0.014. TWO independent predictors both vanish on Championship while means/variance are intact (Championship feature std 0.90, percentiles 2.8/4.0/5.1). D1: adapter orientation correct (raw .home->team_a, .away->team_b; extract_stat reads each team's OWN cards; traced on multiple matches), scale correct (Championship yellows/match 3.96 vs FootyStats 4.04). D2: could not A/B identical fixtures (99 legacy stats files have a match-ID namespace with zero overlap with cached match-lists) - ran the shared-code equivalent instead. D3: thin history RULED OUT - every sanity-gate prediction already had >=19 prior matches per team (median 32); restricting to more history/training moves correlation toward 0 (-0.023 at n_train>=200), never positive. D4: reds under-recorded on Championship (null on 91% of matches, present in 9% vs FootyStats 17%) but immaterial - yellows-only vs yellows+reds changes FootyStats correlation by 0.005.
entries.conclusion: NOT a pipeline bug. The sanity gate correctly detected that the known-good card signal is ABSENT on Championship 25/26. The signal is flat at the raw-feature level (before the model) for two independent predictors, which a shared-code wiring bug could not selectively produce. This is a GENERALIZATION finding: a signal validated across ~25 leagues shows near-zero within-season persistence on this 26th (Championship 25/26) - plausibly because promotion/relegation churn and roster turnover compress team-level disciplinary persistence. It breaks the 'sanity-gate failure = bug' streak (this is the 1 genuine case). Model-side conclusions from the Championship slice (F015) remain untrustworthy AS INTENDED - the gate did its job. CAVEAT: single season, n=275 usable; confirm by repeating the raw-feature correlation on Championship 24/25 (sn_2930227)/23/24, cheap and within existing trial budget. MARKET-CALIBRATION result from F015 is model-independent and unaffected (not re-litigated).

evidence.reds_immaterial: yellows-only vs yellow+red changes FootyStats rho by 0.005

entries.followup: CONFIRMED STRUCTURAL & CARDS-SPECIFIC by F017 (2026-08-29): the flat card signal replicates across Championship 24/25 and 23/24 (not just 25/26), so it is NOT a single-season artifact. And it is cards-specific: goals persistence transfers to Championship at corpus-comparable strength (xG->goals +0.114*/+0.149***), corners is corpus-level. F016's 'genuine finding not a bug' conclusion stands and is strengthened.

entries.title: Championship card-signal failure is STRUCTURAL and CARDS-SPECIFIC — confirmed across 3 seasons; goals signal transfers fine
entries.what_we_tried: F016 found team card/foul predictors flat on Championship 25/26 (raw-feature Spearman, model-free) vs strongly positive on the 25-league corpus, but n=275 on one season was thin for a structural claim. Repeated the IDENTICAL model-free raw-feature correlation (rolling w5, point-in-time, feature=home+away team rolling rate, Spearman vs realized total; NO model/GLM/metric definitions) on Championship 24/25 (sn_2930227) and 23/24 (sn_343481) - full regular seasons, 552 matches each, every team exactly 46 appearances (perfectly balanced). Also measured corners and goals predictors to test whether flatness is cards-specific or league-wide. ~1,116 API requests (fixtures+stats, no odds). Per season, never pooled.
entries.what_happened: CARDS: yellow-card-rate->cards is corpus +0.177*** [.161,.193] but Championship -0.044 (25/26), +0.033 (24/25), +0.012 (23/24) - every CI includes 0 AND excludes corpus +0.177. foul-rate->cards: corpus +0.175*** vs Championship -0.010/-0.030/-0.041. Flat across all 3 seasons, both predictors. GOALS: xG-rate->goals corpus +0.099*** vs Championship +0.114* (25/26)/+0.057/+0.149*** (23/24); SOT-rate->goals corpus +0.107*** vs +0.050/+0.032/+0.135** (23/24) - goals persistence HOLDS at corpus-comparable strength. CORNERS: corpus +0.067*** vs +/-0/+0.087/+0.067 - corpus-level (weak everywhere). Self-check: script reproduces F016 exactly (corpus cards +0.177, 25/26 -0.044) before trusting new seasons.
entries.conclusion: STRUCTURAL, not a single-season artifact: the card/foul->cards signal is flat in all three Championship seasons tested, with every CI excluding the corpus value. And CARDS-SPECIFIC, not a league-wide loss of team signal: goals persistence transfers to Championship at ~corpus strength (so the 'squad churn erases all persistence' mechanism is too broad - it's disciplinary-specific). PRODUCT IMPLICATION: cards-based metrics require per-league validation before deployment and Championship specifically should be EXCLUDED for cards strategies; goals-based team signal does transfer. A signal surviving cumulative FDR across ~25 leagues is NOT evidence it holds in a 26th - generalization must be measured (cheaply, via this model-free raw-feature check) before modelling/odds spend. Does NOT change the F015 market-calibration/buy conclusion (model-independent, untouched). Strengthens F016 (genuine finding, not a bug).

evidence.method: model-free raw-feature Spearman, rolling w5, point-in-time, per season never pooled

entries.title: Multi-source discovery (24 new TheStatsAPI fields, 3 second-tier leagues): NO survivor — broader claim now tested, not just the narrow one
entries.what_we_tried: Every prior discovery (cards/goals/BTTS/corners) ran on FootyStats basic stats only, so prior negatives supported only the NARROW claim 'metrics from basic public stats don't beat the market'. For the first time we searched the ~24 TheStatsAPI-unique fields (blocked_shots, shots_inside/outside_box, big_chances(_missed), touches_in_penalty_area, final_third_entries, accurate_crosses/long_balls, the duels family, the defending family tackles/interceptions/clearances/ball_recoveries, goalkeeping, np_expected_goals, half-splits) across English Championship, French Ligue 2, Spanish La Liga 2. 6-step protocol: (1) BLOCKING merge-validation gate FootyStats<->TheStatsAPI on shared fields; (2) balanced corpus (Championship cached 3 seasons; freshly pulled Ligue2 comp_9777 25/26+24/25 = 306+306 and LaLiga2 comp_0976 25/26+24/25 = 462+462, full regular seasons so every team equal appearances) + per-league field-population; (3) per-league/target sanity gate (raw-feature model-free then model-based), search only where it passes; (4) discovery = small 2-feature Poisson GLM+L2 over point-in-time rolling features, bounded mechanism-motivated candidate pools, cumulative BH-FDR; (5) EV vs cached Bet365 odds + model-independent market BSS; (6) honest report. No model substitution/refit of the 7 metrics; held-out untouched. ~1,774 live requests (2 seasons + 18 fixtures + 1,534 stats + 218 odds).
entries.what_happened: STEP 1 merge PASSED decisively: on the Championship 24/25 overlap season (present in both sources) the crosswalk join agrees 95.0% (cards)/97.6% (corners) exact vs a 21.8% shuffled namespace-mismatch null (73pt gap); SOT/fouls lower agreement (82-89%) is provider measurement noise on subjective fields, not a join error (F016/D2 namespace issue was about raw match-ID matching, which this join does not use). STEP 3 GATE (search only where it passes): PASS = champ/goals (model rho +0.113), ligue2/cards (+0.141), laliga2/cards (+0.181); FAIL/untestable = champ/cards (EXPECTED per F017), champ/corners, ligue2/goals (weak SOT + xG absent), laliga2/goals (xG null in 24/25 blocks model confirmation), all corners. STEP 4: bounded family (cards 144 / goals 196 / corners 64 models x 2 lines); 968 NEW candidates over the 3 gate-passing cells; cumulative FDR family 22855 -> 23823; 484 computable candidates screened; ZERO survived BH correction. Strongest raw signals all LaLiga2/cards defensive-engagement (tackles+fouls Spearman +0.156 p<0.0001) but none clear the 23823-member family. 7-metric re-test: no demotions (already TESTED_NEGATIVE/priced-in; still non-survivors under enlarged family); LaLiga2 cards metrics detectable uncorrected (+0.18-0.19) but that is not the bar. STEP 5: no survivors to EV-test; the DECISIVE odds-coverage gap is that Bet365 offers NO total_cards market for Ligue2 (0/108) or LaLiga2 (1/110) - the two leagues where cards persistence exists have no cards market to monetize. Market BSS vs naive (model-independent): goals EPL-like (goals@2.5 +3.65%/+1.81%, orr 4.5-6.8%), corners@9.5 -0.50%/-2.56% (orr ~8%) - second-tier not measurably sloppier than EPL.
entries.conclusion: NO exploitable, multiple-testing-robust edge from the new fields in these leagues. This is a MUCH STRONGER negative than prior runs because the ~24 TheStatsAPI-unique fields were finally searched: the broader claim ('richer proprietary stats don't beat the market either'), not just the narrow one, is now tested and holds. TWO by-products worth held-out confirmation (NOT validated findings): (1) cards disciplinary-persistence is LEAGUE-SPECIFIC, not tier-specific - present in Ligue2 & LaLiga2, flat only in the Championship - which REFINES F017 (Championship-specific, not a down-tier property); (2) the strongest new-field signal is defensive-engagement -> cards in LaLiga2 (tackles/fouls/clearances/ball_recoveries), a near-miss under FDR with no Bet365 cards market to exploit. Wide CIs (per-cell n 300-900); a positive point estimate that doesn't clear the cumulative family is a hypothesis, not a result. Does NOT change F015 (market calibration/buy: second-tier EPL-like, down-tier thesis unsupported) or F016; refines F017. Held-out set untouched.

evidence.best_near_miss: laliga2/cards tackles_w10 + fouls_w10, Spearman +0.156, p<0.0001 (does not clear family 23823)
evidence.cards_persistence_league_specific: present Ligue2 (+0.141) & LaLiga2 (+0.181); flat Championship (refines F017)
evidence.bet365_sharp_caveat: market-referenced results are a conservative lower bound vs softer books (bc.game); untested, not overstated; moot here (no survivors, no cards market)
evidence.per_team_balance: full regular seasons; Champ 24x46, Ligue2 18x34, LaLiga2 22x42

entries.title: Same-game correlation-gap hypothesis: DISPROVEN at Step 1 — cards/corners/goals outcomes are near-zero (slightly NEGATIVE) correlated, uniform across profiles; market gap untestable (no cached same-game combo prices)
entries.what_we_tried: Tested whether same-game cross-market combinations (cards×corners, cards×goals, corners×goals) carry a real modelling gap: whether the TRUE joint probability is materially higher than a bookmaker's blanket correlation adjustment in identifiable match profiles, by enough to clear the same-game overround (15-25%). Step 1: measured model-free realized pairwise correlation (Pearson+Spearman) across the full corpus (15,359 complete matches, 15,335 with valid corners, 50 league-seasons), broken down by referee card tendency (look-ahead-free expanding-window terciles), tempo (dangerous-attacks terciles), competitive balance (|home_ppg-away_ppg| median split), and league. Every pooled correlation reported alongside a within-league-season z-scored version to rule out a Simpson/league-mix artifact. Pre-stated gate. Step 2 (only to serve Step 5): built the joint by coupling the VALIDATED CountRegressionModel marginals (Poisson/NB+L2+team shrinkage) with a Gaussian copula (latent rho=2 sin(pi rho_s/6)); chose copula over bivariate-Poisson because measured corr is near-zero AND negative and Holgate biv-Poisson only represents positive corr; marginal-recovery sanity gate. Step 3: naive P(A)xP(B) vs joint, plus market-coverage check. Zero API calls; NO refit/substitution of the marginals (F009 lesson); held-out untouched.
entries.what_happened: GATE FAILED AT STEP 1. Overall within-league-season Spearman: cards×corners -0.033 (95% CI [-0.049,-0.017]), cards×goals -0.030 [-0.046,-0.014], corners×goals -0.028 [-0.044,-0.012]; pooled -0.047/-0.043/-0.019; Pearson near-identical. All THREE are near-zero and NEGATIVE — the opposite sign to the hypothesis premise ('high-tempo physical match produces both cards and corners'). Multiple-testing family = 60 profile-bucket×pair correlation tests. Criterion A (overall positive & |rho|>=0.05): FALSE. Criterion B (any bucket positive, >=+0.10, BH-significant): FALSE — 0 positive-and-BH-significant buckets; 6 negative-and-BH-significant. Profile variation is small under the within-league-season control (referee 0.02-0.06 range, tempo 0.01-0.02, balance up to 0.065 but both sides ~0/negative). The single positive-looking slice (league 12325 cards×corners +0.117, n=380) does NOT survive BH — the exact multiple-comparison false positive the brief anticipated. STEP 2 sanity gate PASSED (marginal recovery 1e-9 << 1e-6; copula validated to ~1e-16 vs scipy). STEP 3 naive-vs-joint (Over∩Over, cards O3.5/corners O9.5/goals O2.5): joint is BELOW naive everywhere — cards×corners naive 29.58% vs joint 28.94% (-0.64pp, -2.5% rel), cards×goals 30.70% vs 30.06% (-0.63pp), corners×goals 27.12% vs 26.84% (-0.29pp); max abs gap over 15k matches <=0.78pp; by-profile movement <0.05pp. MARKET COMPARISON UNTESTABLE: 0 of 420 cached odds files contain a same-game COMBINATION price for any target cross-market pair; only total_goals_btts (10) and correct_score (10) exist, both goals-internal. Single-market overrounds (Bet365): goals@2.5 5.3%, cards ~7.9-8.0%, corners ~8.2%.
entries.conclusion: DISPROVEN, and closed at the correlation-structure step. At the match-total level the cards/corners/goals outcomes are effectively independent (near-zero) with a slight NEGATIVE coupling, and this is uniform across referee/tempo/balance/league profiles once the league-mix artifact is controlled. There is no positive, material, multiple-testing-robust correlation for a joint model to exploit, so a bookmaker's blanket correlation adjustment is approximately correct — there is no gap. TWO standalone honest deliverables: (1) The market-gap question is FORMALLY UNTESTABLE with cached data — no same-game combination prices for the target pairs are cached — reported as a hard limitation, not worked around. (2) STEP 5 (required regardless): modelling the joint instead of multiplying marginals changes the combined Over∩Over probability by <1pp (~1-2.5% relative) and in the direction of a slightly LOWER joint; so P(A)xP(B) is a good approximation for these markets, wrong by ~1pp on the high side. Net of overround (>=8% per single leg, more for a combo), a <=0.8pp WRONG-SIGN gap cannot be an edge. Consistent with the project's accumulated finding that these markets' signal is already priced/at-par (F002/F003/F013). CAVEATS: model-free correlations are tight (CIs exclude the hypothesized values); copula divergence is descriptive (inherits validated marginals), computed on full corpus, not an edge claim; held-out untouched. Confirmation of the market-gap leg would require cached/fresh same-game combination prices, which do not exist in this dataset.

entries.title: Raw-observable-stats engine (clean run, no prior metrics): sanity gate exposed a mis-specified feature instrument; after fixing it, the only FDR survivors were a pooling (Simpson) artifact with zero within-league significance. No genuine raw-stat edge found.
entries.what_we_tried: Built a market-independent prediction engine on RAW observable match stats only (goals/corners/cards/fouls/shots/SOT/xG/possession/dangerous-attacks + referee expanding card&foul rates), no reference to any prior discovered metric. Systematic mechanism-restricted search over size-1/2/3 feature sets (same-stat persistence, cross-stat, cross-team interaction, referee-conditioned, style/tempo) across 25 leagues x 9 target/line cells, Poisson/logistic with shrinkage, walk-forward point-in-time, sanity-gate-first, cumulative-FDR corrected against family 23,823. Also probed a heatmap spatial batch.
entries.what_happened: (1) The reused slot-based rolling features (team_a_*/team_b_*) were MIS-SPECIFIED as team instruments (they conflate team identity with home/away venue); the sanity gate correctly FAILED even pooled (xG->goals corr 0.004). Rebuilding team-consistent point-in-time features restored the known-good signal (xG->goals corr 0.109; pooled gate PASS for goals/cards/btts/clean-sheet). Corners failed the gate even pooled (persistence ~0) and was marked untestable, matching the known structural null. (2) Per-league, every gate failed (n~300/league gives train ~187/test ~217 - too little power); pooled the search tested 46 gate-passed candidates -> cumulative family 23,823 -> 23,869; 24 cleared the cumulative BH rank-1 threshold (p<=2.09e-6), led by referee-card-tendency x both-teams-foul-rate -> cards (pooled BSS +4.30%). (3) DECISIVE: per-league breakdown showed 0 of 24 pooled survivors are significant (p<0.05) in even ONE individual league, and cards-persistence pooled +2.27% is NEGATIVE in all 8 testable leagues (EPL -4.31%). The pooled significance is a between-league base-rate (Simpson) artifact, not within-league predictive signal. (4) Heatmap: all 4 candidate spatial endpoints returned 404 - no heatmap data exists on this plan; no batch run.
entries.conclusion: No genuine raw-stat predictive edge was found. The pooled FDR survivors are a pooling confound and were NOT promoted to held-out (held-out set untouched). The most valuable output is methodological: (a) the sanity gate again caught a mis-specified instrument (the 8th such catch); (b) per-league evaluation is mandatory - pooled search over leagues with different base rates manufactures spurious significance; (c) at ~300 matches/league the engine has insufficient power to detect the small (BSS ~1-2%) within-league signal that genuinely exists for cards/goals. Corners persistence remains ~0 (untestable). Heatmap spatial data is unavailable (endpoint 404). Cumulative FDR family updated 23,823 -> 23,869.
entries.evidence: scripts/raw_stats_discovery.py, data/discovery/raw_stats_discovery.json (pooled_gates, per_league_consistency_of_pooled_survivors: n_pooled_survivors=24, n_sig_in_any_league=0), scripts/heatmap_fetch.py, data/thestatsapi/heatmap/_probe_result.json (all endpoints 404), docs/raw_stats_engine_report.md. Quota: 4 live requests spent on heatmap probe (monthly_remaining 5518 -> 5514); core run zero API.
